title: Ecosystem Sentinel — continuous competitive model signals & procurement heuristics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight, continuously-updating 'Ecosystem Sentinel' that synthesizes upstream signals about open and commercial LLMs into actionable procurement heuristics for PM/Procurement/Platform teams. The sentinel will combine availability notices, licensing changes, release feature flags (function-calling, streaming, quantization/8-bit support), latency/cost archetypes, regional/hardware affinity, and vendor outage telemetry to produce: 1) a model risk/availability score, 2) a time-to-fallback estimate, and 3) an automated procurement trigger recommendation. Goal: reduce manual model-scouting time and provide deterministic triggers for when to push Dedicated/Private procurement conversations or adjustment of routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: Data pipeline ingests at least 6 signal sources (vendor release notes, model registry crawls, public infra status pages, telemetry-derived latency/cost deltas, licensing trackers, and curated research feeds) on a daily cadence
Scorecard computes Model Availability Score and Procurement Urgency for each tracked model with reproducible formula that is documented in Confluence
Dashboard (Grafana/Metabase) exposes top-10 at-risk models, delta-trend charts, and automatic alerts when Procurement Urgency >= threshold
Runbook defines 3 canonical responses (routing policy change, reserve Dedicated capacity, start Private onboarding) and maps triggers to stakeholders
Playbook validated in a 1-week simulated outage tabletop with Product, Infra, and Sales and feedback loop incorporated
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: scoped MVP to 12 target models (mix of open-source and hosted competitors). Agreed daily ingestion, weekly scoring refresh. (Aisha)

2026-03-05 — Data engineering prototyped a feed that scrapes vendor release notes and public status pages; initial schema v0.1 committed (GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-sentinel/pr/58). (Diego)
2026-03-08 — PM review: reduced initial signal set to prioritize availability + latency + license changes. Decision: postpone deep quantization compatibility until phase 2 to reduce scope.
2026-03-10 — Design: created dashboard wireframe (Drive: drive.google.com/rd/inference/sentinel-wireframe). Feedback: show both relative risk and estimated cost-to-fallback.
2026-03-12 — Infra noted dependency on telemetry pipeline (ENG-48231). Added dependency and tagged data retention SLA requirement. (Diego)

2026-03-14 — Implemented scoring prototype and ran backtest against last quarter of incidents; observed recall=0.78 for major availability events, false positives concentrated in models with frequent minor releases. Next: tune thresholds and add suppression rules. (Aisha)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: breadth vs. signal quality. Chose higher precision for procurement triggers to avoid churning sales conversations.
If prototype shows >30% false positive rate in thresholds, phase 1 will be limited to internal ops alerts only (no customer-facing guidance).

Potential follow-ups: integrate with routing policies to auto-fall back to pinned model variants; export alerts to Slack and PagerDuty; quantify cost of reserving Dedicated capacity vs. pay-as-you-go during outage windows.
